main.title: Split/Second
main.subtitle: Racing on a set built to collapse
main.summary: Split/Second: Velocity (released in North America as Split/Second) is a racing video game developed by Black Rock Studio and published by Disney Interactive Studios for Windows, PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 in May 2010.

cards.heading: Racing on a set built to collapse
cards.text: Split/Second: Velocity (released in North America as Split/Second) is a racing video game developed by Black Rock Studio and published by Disney Interactive Studios for Windows, PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 in May 2010. In the game, players take part in a fictional reality television show consisting of a variety of events, each focusing on destructible environments triggered remotely by driver actions known as "power plays".

cards.heading: Driving charges the power play
cards.text: In Split/Second, players take part in a fictional reality TV programme where participants race for money and fame. Throughout a race, players can build up their "power play" meter by performing stunts, such as jumps and mid-air overtakes, and precision driving, such as drafting opponents and drifting. As players build up their meter, special events can be triggered, which create obstacles for other players, open up temporary shortcuts, or alter an entire section of the race course. These triggers are also activated by the AI opponents.

cards.heading: Choosing when to change the track
cards.text: Such events range from shockwave-inducing explosions to buckling highways and dam breaches. The severity of the events available to trigger varies depending on how full the player's meter is. The Level 1 events become available when one or two of the three segments of the bar are full, while the Level 2 events can only be triggered upon a full bar. Event locations, and the vehicles they will affect, are highlighted with blue icons for the level one power plays, and red icons for level two, and the player must time the action accurately in order to hinder the opposition as much as possible. The power play meter is used up by one segment once a level one event is triggered, so the player must also choose whether to activate the less destructive first-level events as soon as they are available, or save the power play energy and build it up further in order to trigger the top-tier actions.

cards.heading: An interface behind the car
cards.text: There are also certain power plays that can be reused, such as explosives dropped from helicopters, exploding tankers, and shortcuts, but some other power plays are permanent and can only be used once in a single race. Black Rock Studio also wanted to make the HUD as simple as possible by taking away all unnecessary elements such as the speedometer and the track map (rendered useless due to the dynamic nature of the track) leaving only the lap count (also the target time in "Detonator" and "Air Revenge" modes as well as target score in "Air Strike" and "Survival" modes), the position that the player is in, and the power play meter, all positioned behind the player's car to avoid detracting from the scenery.

main.title: Prince of Persia: The Forgotten Sands
main.subtitle: A return to the Sands of Time
main.summary: Prince of Persia: The Forgotten Sands refers to a group of 2010 action-adventure games developed and published by Ubisoft, with each version handled by different internal teams.

cards.heading: A return to the Sands of Time
cards.text: Prince of Persia: The Forgotten Sands refers to a group of 2010 action-adventure games developed and published by Ubisoft, with each version handled by different internal teams. The main version was developed for PlayStation 3, Xbox 360 and Windows; other versions were developed for Nintendo DS, PlayStation Portable, mobile and web browsers, and a notable version for the Wii. It forms part of the Prince of Persia series, and is set within the continuity of Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time (2003).

cards.heading: Acrobatics across the palace
cards.text: In the PlayStation 3, Xbox 360 and Windows game, the Prince crosses a large palace complex using wall-runs, climbing, beam-balancing and pole-swinging. Traps interrupt those routes, while groups of enemies occupy arena encounters. Magical powers supplement the acrobatics as the adventure progresses.

cards.heading: Water and time become tools
cards.text: The Prince's powers turn parts of the environment into routes. Water can be frozen into a wall or pole, while Earth restores destroyed structures. A limited rewind allows a mistaken jump or damaging encounter to be reconsidered. Wind and Fire add offensive options when groups of enemies close in, with dodges and rolls making room between attacks. Defeated enemies supply experience for stronger abilities and health. The adventure therefore develops by expanding both the Prince's movement through a space and his answers when that space fills with opponents.

main.title: Red Dead Redemption
main.subtitle: John Marston at the end of the frontier
main.summary: Rockstar released Red Dead Redemption in North America for PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 on May 18, 2010, with Europe following three days later.

cards.heading: Marston returns to his past
cards.text: Rockstar released Red Dead Redemption for PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 in North America on May 18, 2010. John Marston crosses a frontier of ranches, towns and deserts while federal agents force him to hunt former companions. Railways, cars and official power are changing the world in which he once lived as an outlaw.

cards.heading: The frontier in 1911
cards.text: The 1911 setting brings revolvers and ranches alongside trains, telegraphs and automobiles. Marston's past belongs to a frontier now increasingly controlled by modern institutions. That conflict shapes both the missions he receives and the places he visits.

cards.heading: Crossing the land on horseback
cards.text: Travelling by horse leaves time to notice changing light, animals and other travellers. A quiet journey can be interrupted by a chance encounter, or remain still enough to emphasise isolation. Crossing the distance between settlements gives the landscape a pace different from travelling through a modern city.

cards.heading: Picking targets with Dead Eye
cards.text: Dead Eye slows time and allows the player to mark targets before firing. It turns a crowded gunfight into a sequence of deliberate shots. Because the ability consumes a limited resource, the player must choose when its advantage is most useful.

main.title: Super Mario Galaxy 2
main.summary: Super Mario Galaxy 2 is a 2010 platform game developed and published by Nintendo for the Wii.

cards.text: Super Mario Galaxy 2 is a 2010 platform game developed and published by Nintendo for the Wii. It was first announced at E3 2009 and is the sequel to 2007's Super Mario Galaxy. Much like the first game, the story follows Mario as he pursues the Koopa King, Bowser, into outer space, where he has imprisoned Princess Peach and taken control of the universe using Power Stars and Grand Stars. Mario must travel across various galaxies to recover the Power Stars in order to travel to the center of the universe and rescue Princess Peach.

The game was originally planned as an updated version of Super Mario Galaxy, known as Super Mario Galaxy More. However, it was later decided that the game would be expanded into a fully fleshed-out sequel when the development staff continued to build upon the game with dozens of new ideas. As such, development time expanded to two and a half years. The sequel features dynamic environments, new power-ups and Yoshi.

Super Mario Galaxy 2 was met with critical acclaim, and was considered to match or surpass its lauded predecessor, with its creativity, level design, gameplay, music, and technological improvements over the original receiving high praise, although critics were divided on its lack of story and high difficulty compared to the original. It is frequently regarded by critics to be one of the greatest video games ever made and is one of the best-selling games on the Wii, with over seven million copies sold worldwide.

The sequel's later editions brought its galaxies to another generation of players. An enhanced Nintendo Switch collection reunited it with Super Mario Galaxy, adding display and interface improvements alongside an assist mode and storybook content.

main.title: Alpha Protocol
main.summary: Obsidian's espionage role-playing game follows rogue agent Michael Thorton through a conspiracy shaped by missions, relationships and timed dialogue choices.

cards.heading: Michael Thorton becomes a rogue agent
cards.text: Alpha Protocol is a 2010 action role-playing game developed by Obsidian Entertainment and published by Sega. The player assumes control of agent Michael Thorton, a new recruit at a clandestine United States agency called Alpha Protocol, which is given unlimited resources to conduct covert operations on behalf of the government. Thorton becomes a rogue agent and must unravel an international conspiracy to stop a war. Throughout the game, players must make many choices that affect the narrative. Played from a third-person perspective, players can confront enemies using firearms, gadgets, martial arts and stealth. The game features extensive customization and a dialogue stance system that allows players to select dialogues based on three different tones.

cards.heading: Choose Thorton's background and appearance
cards.text: Alpha Protocol is an action role-playing game played from a third-person perspective. Players assume control of Michael Thorton, a secret agent who must travel around the world as he unravels a conspiracy that threatens his safety. At the start of the game, players can choose Thorton's agent history; options include Soldiers—which focuses on using heavy firearms, Tech Specialists—which have an arsenal of gadgets to use, and Field Agents—which encourages the use of stealth. There are also Freelancer, Recruit, and Veteran options, in which players custom-build their own class. Players can customize elements of Thorton's appearance, including his hair, eye color, costumes, and accessories including hats and glasses.

cards.heading: Stealth, gadgets and firearms shape each mission
cards.text: Safe houses provide a place to choose missions, buy intelligence and equipment, and modify weapons. Objectives can be approached with firearms, gadgets, martial arts or stealth, with multiple paths through levels. Locks, computers and alarms use minigames, while collected money funds later preparations. Equipment and information bought before a mission can alter the options available during it.

cards.heading: A timed conversation can change the story
cards.text: Conversations continue in real time, leaving limited time to choose a response. Professional, suave and aggressive stances affect each character differently. Intelligence dossiers can open additional options, and a contact's opinion of Thorton can help or undermine later operations. Decisions about individual characters also change the direction of the story, with some consequences appearing well after the conversation.

cards.heading: Obsidian develops an espionage role-playing game
cards.text: The game's development began in March 2006 after publisher Sega approached Obsidian for a new intellectual property role-playing game. While Obsidian co-founders Feargus Urquhart and Chris Jones came up with the concept of an "espionage RPG", no one was assigned to lead the project until early 2008. The project was mostly inspired by iconic spy characters such as Jason Bourne, James Bond and Jack Bauer, and by films including Syriana, Ronin and The Good, the Bad and the Ugly. Sega also participated in the game's development, supporting the plot rewrite by Chris Avellone, and sending quality assurance and cohesion strike teams to ensure there were no plot holes.

main.title: Snoopy Flying Ace
main.subtitle: Snoopy's flying fantasy becomes an arcade dogfight
main.summary: Snoopy Flying Ace is Smart Bomb Interactive's Xbox Live Arcade flight-combat game, released on 2 June 2010. It places the Peanuts cast inside a stylised First World War setting, with Snoopy facing the Red Baron and his Flying Circus. Biplanes and triplanes become the means of fast, accessible aerial contests rather than a detailed simulation of historical flying. The player performs evasive manoeuvres, pursues opponents and selects weapons while the familiar characters give the fighting an immediately recognisable comic identity. Two players can also take the entire campaign on together through split-screen cooperation.

cards.heading: Snoopy's flying fantasy becomes an arcade dogfight
cards.text: Snoopy Flying Ace is Smart Bomb Interactive's Xbox Live Arcade flight-combat game, released on 2 June 2010. It places the Peanuts cast inside a stylised First World War setting, with Snoopy facing the Red Baron and his Flying Circus. Biplanes and triplanes become the means of fast, accessible aerial contests rather than a detailed simulation of historical flying. The player performs evasive manoeuvres, pursues opponents and selects weapons while the familiar characters give the fighting an immediately recognisable comic identity. Two players can also take the entire campaign on together through split-screen cooperation.

cards.heading: A plane carries more than its machine guns
cards.text: Aircraft can be customised visually and equipped with additional weapons, including missiles, floating mines and an electromagnetic blast. Barrel rolls and other acrobatic manoeuvres help change direction or escape an attack. Flying into a stationary turret provides another position from which to join the fight. The player therefore reads the space for useful equipment and angles as well as nearby enemies. After respawning, weapons can be changed to suit a different approach, making another attempt an opportunity to alter the tools brought into the same crowded section of sky.

cards.heading: The comic cast supports a substantial multiplayer game
cards.text: Online modes supported up to sixteen players, from conventional dogfights to Pigskin, an airborne ball game whose scoring depends on passing between aircraft. Peanuts characters, costumes and Xbox avatars gave players several ways to personalise their pilots. Successful streaks could even bring Woodstock onto the plane to attack enemies behind it. Reviews praised the amount of content and the polished arcade action. Snoopy Flying Ace makes the licence useful through a clear fantasy already associated with its hero, turning the imagined Flying Ace into a coherent flight game with room for cooperative and competitive play.

main.title: Green Day: Rock Band
main.subtitle: Green Day's career on the Rock Band stage
main.summary: On June 8, 2010 Harmonix devoted the entire Rock Band format to Green Day.

cards.heading: Green Day takes the stage
cards.text: Harmonix released Green Day: Rock Band on June 8, 2010. Guitar, bass, drums and vocal parts follow the band through different stages of its career, with period costumes and venues accompanying the songs. Career challenges unlock photographs and videos from the disc.

cards.heading: Career challenges and the drum trainer
cards.text: Career mode makes the available songs accessible from the start. Completing themed challenges and earning strong ratings unlocks rewards and further challenges. Quickplay provides direct access to songs outside Career. The drum trainer includes common rhythms and Tr? Cool's patterns and solos, letting players practise parts separately.

cards.heading: Four players perform different parts
cards.text: Green Day: Rock Band allows players to perform simulated rock music by providing up to four players with the ability to play three different controllers modeled after music instruments: a guitar controller for lead guitar and bass guitar gameplay, a drum controller and a microphone for vocals. Players simulate performances by using their controllers to play scrolling notes. For lead and bass guitar, this is accomplished by holding down colored buttons mimicking guitar frets and pushing the controller's strum bar. For drums, this requires striking the matching colored drumhead, or stepping on the pedal to simulate playing bass drum notes. When singing vocals, the player must sing in relative pitch to the original vocals. A pitch indicator displays the singer's accuracy relative to the original pitch. The game supports harmonies as introduced in The Beatles: Rock Band, allowing multiple singers to perform the vocal portion. Harmonies will be added to the six songs already available as downloadable content for the game when played in Green Day: Rock Band.

cards.heading: Venues from different stages of Green Day's history
cards.text: Three venues mark different periods. The Warehouse is a fictional composite of early clubs and house parties for Dookie. Milton Keynes' National Bowl accompanies American Idiot and other albums, recalling the Bullet in a Bible performance. Oakland's Fox Theatre presents 21st Century Breakdown, drawing on the band's 2009 show there.

main.title: Xenoblade Chronicles
main.summary: Xenoblade Chronicles is an action role-playing game developed by Monolith Soft and published by Nintendo for the Wii.

cards.heading: A role-playing world reaches the Wii
cards.text: Monolith Soft developed Xenoblade Chronicles for Wii, published by Nintendo in Japan in 2010, PAL regions in 2011 and North America in 2012. Its large connected zones combine side quests, relationships between party members and real-time battles. Shulk's glimpses of the future become part of combat decisions. The original later reached New Nintendo 3DS, followed by the expanded Definitive Edition for Nintendo Switch.

cards.heading: A journey across the bodies of titans
cards.text: Xenoblade Chronicles takes place on the frozen bodies of two warring titans, the Bionis and the Mechonis. The people of the Bionis, including the human-like Homs, are at perpetual war with the Mechon, a mechanical race of the Mechonis. Key to the Homs' efforts in fighting against the Mechon is the Monado, a sword said to have once been wielded by the Bionis. During an attack on his colony, the main protagonist Shulk discovers his ability to wield the Monado and sets out on a quest for revenge with his best friend, Reyn, with others joining in as the game progresses.

cards.heading: A physical model becomes a setting
cards.text: The concept for Xenoblade Chronicles originated in June 2006, when the game's executive director and lead writer, Tetsuya Takahashi, visualized and constructed a model of two giant titans frozen in place, with people living on their bodies. Development began in 2007 under the title Monado: Beginning of the World, though it was eventually rebranded with its current title to honor Takahashi's previous work on the Xeno series. The script was worked on by Takahashi, anime writer Yuichiro Takeda, and Nintendo writer Yurie Hattori. The music was handled by six different composers, including first-timer and lead composer Manami Kiyota and industry veterans Yoko Shimomura and Yasunori Mitsuda, with the latter also writing the ending theme, "Beyond the Sky".

cards.heading: Regional releases and a campaign for access
cards.text: The game was announced in 2009 under its original title and released in Japan the following year. Despite releasing in Europe and in Oceania, its North American release remained unconfirmed until December 2011, when a fan campaign called Operation Rainfall drew attention to the game. Upon release, the game was critically acclaimed as one of the best recent role-playing games, while its New Nintendo 3DS port was praised for successfully re-creating the game in a portable form. It was particularly praised for its story, which critics called innovative and surprisingly complex, and was commercially successful in both Japan and the West. In the years since its release, it has been considered one of the best video games of all time. A spiritual successor by the same development team for the Wii U, Xenoblade Chronicles X, was released in April 2015. A sequel for the Nintendo Switch, Xenoblade Chronicles 2, was released in December 2017. A third entry, Xenoblade Chronicles 3, was released in July 2022, also on the Nintendo Switch.

main.title: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective
main.subtitle: Investigate your own death
main.summary: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective is Capcom's Nintendo DS puzzle adventure about Sissel, a ghost who has lost the memory of his life and death. Over a single night he follows a chain of people in danger, using supernatural powers to discover what connects them. Directed and written by Shu Takumi, it turns a murder mystery into a sequence of physical interventions. Sissel cannot simply question everyone or walk through the city. He has to understand the objects around him well enough to make the living world respond.

cards.heading: Investigate your own death
cards.text: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective is Capcom's Nintendo DS puzzle adventure about Sissel, a ghost who has lost the memory of his life and death. Over a single night he follows a chain of people in danger, using supernatural powers to discover what connects them. Directed and written by Shu Takumi, it turns a murder mystery into a sequence of physical interventions. Sissel cannot simply question everyone or walk through the city. He has to understand the objects around him well enough to make the living world respond.

cards.heading: A route made from ordinary objects
cards.text: In the Ghost World, time stops and Sissel can move between the cores of nearby objects. Returning to the real world lets him perform a trick with the object he possesses, such as shifting something into another character's path. That action may create access to a new core or change what somebody does next. A room is consequently both a collection of mechanisms and a route through space. The player has to consider what an object can do before deciding whether its position can lead somewhere useful.

cards.heading: Four minutes to change an outcome
cards.text: Sissel can return to the four minutes before a person's death and try to prevent it. Repeated observation reveals the sequence of movements that produces the fatal result, allowing a small intervention to redirect it. Failure becomes information for another attempt rather than the end of the investigation. The expressive animation makes those sequences readable and gives the characters a strong physical personality. Ghost Trick builds its mystery through consequences: changing the position of one ordinary thing can save a life and uncover another part of the night's larger explanation.
